**Finding: deviation (Section 10.3, ¶p0063) — redline validated and submitted.**

- **What the document says:** Section 10.3 is a bare successors-and-assigns clause with no consent mechanic. There is no change-of-control language anywhere in the agreement, and the Section 4 termination provisions give HDI only the mutual 90-day termination right — no CoC trigger.
- **Where it stands vs. the playbook:** Two limbs are fine and were not touched — our assignment freedom is unrestricted, and HDI has no termination/re-pricing right on our change of control (so no walk-away issue). But the total absence of a consent standard lets HDI assign this hosting arrangement to anyone, including a competitor, which fails even the fallback ("consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld").
- **Fix:** One appended sentence set adding the affiliate/successor carve-out for us, a not-unreasonably-withheld consent requirement plus competitor bar on HDI, and confirmation that our change of control is not an assignment. Fallback of a mutual notice-and-consent formulation flagged in the comment.
